t: Lesson 8 — Step 6: the reservoir and the stack light
html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 8 is this chapter: it checks that this lesson’s tags are made, that S6_Supply exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • The reservoir inlet opens at the low float

The filler draws every charge from its head tank, and the head tank tops itself up from the reservoir, Supply_Tank, which nothing refills yet: run step 5 long enough and the line stalls with the tube down, waiting for a charge that never comes. This step keeps the filler fed, so it comes straight after it. Add the JSR above JSR(S3_Index) and write:

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 is a seal-in on the floats: the low float opens the inlet valve, and the valve stays open until the high float. Rung 1 protects the fill: if the filler’s head tank runs low (the reservoir empty, the inlet too slow) the line is stopped rather than pouring short charges. Rungs 2–4 drive the stack light on the tank: red flashing at the low float (the light is set to flash its red segment), amber while refilling, green when healthy and not refilling.

Run it

The tank starts at 35 %: watch it fall a little with every charge (a trend of Supply_Level, chapter 11), reach 20 %, the red flash, the inlet valve open and the level climb to 90 %. Set the reservoir’s Inlet flow to 10 and the line will eventually stop on rung 1; the Simulator Log says why.

Try it

Make amber mean head-tank low instead of refilling. Then fit the reservoir’s flow meter (a setting; it adds an analog input) and trend Supply_Flow against the charges.

rungs.head: S6_Supply · Rung 0
rungs.comment: RESERVOIR: the low float opens the inlet and it seals in until the high float. The filler head tank is topped up from the reservoir by itself: watch Supply_Level fall a little with every charge (fit the reservoir’s flow meter for a Supply_Flow analog too)

pred.q: Supply_Low is off, Supply_Inlet is on, Supply_High is off and Line_Run is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Supply_Inlet is on.

rungs.words: When either (Supply_Low (Supply_Tank low float) is on) or (Supply_Inlet (Supply_Tank inlet valve) is on), Supply_High (Supply_Tank high float) is off and Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, the rung turns Supply_Inlet on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Supply_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Supply_Inlet) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Inlet is on.
  2. XIO(Supply_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Supply_High is off.
  3. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  4. OTE(Supply_Inlet) Output Energize does: turns Supply_Inlet on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Supply_Inlet on, and Supply_Inlet’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: S6_Supply · Rung 1
rungs.comment: PROTECT THE FILL: if the head tank runs low (reservoir empty, inlet too slow) stop the line rather than pour short charges. Try it: set the Supply_Tank Inlet flow to 10 and see this rung trip
rungs.words: When Tank_Low (Filler head tank below 15 %) is on and Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, the rung unlatches Line_Run.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Tank_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tank_Low is on.
  2. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  3. OTU(Line_Run) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Line_Run. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Line_Run when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: S6_Supply · Rung 2
rungs.comment: TANK STACK LIGHT, RED: the reservoir is at its low float (the light is set to flash its red segment)

pred.q: Supply_Low is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Tank_Red is off. It stops at XIC(Supply_Low).

rungs.words: When Supply_Low (Supply_Tank low float) is on, the rung turns Tank_Red (Tank_Light red: reservoir at the low float (flashes)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Supply_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Low is on.
  2. OTE(Tank_Red) Output Energize does: turns Tank_Red on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S6_Supply · Rung 3
rungs.comment: AMBER: the inlet is open, the reservoir is refilling
rungs.words: When Supply_Inlet (Supply_Tank inlet valve) is on, the rung turns Tank_Amber (Tank_Light amber: inlet open, refilling) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Supply_Inlet) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Inlet is on.
  2. OTE(Tank_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Tank_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S6_Supply · Rung 4
rungs.comment: GREEN: level healthy and not refilling. Try it: make amber mean head-tank low instead

pred.q: Supply_Low is off and Supply_Inlet is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Tank_Green is on.

rungs.words: When Supply_Low (Supply_Tank low float) is off and Supply_Inlet (Supply_Tank inlet valve) is off, the rung turns Tank_Green (Tank_Light green: level healthy) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Supply_Low) Examine If Open asks: true when Supply_Low is off.
  2. XIO(Supply_Inlet) Examine If Open asks: true when Supply_Inlet is off.
  3. OTE(Tank_Green) Output Energize does: turns Tank_Green on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
